Problem: Given that the domain of f(x) is R, y=f(2x-1) is an odd function, and y=f(x+1) is an even function, and knowing that f(x)=e^x when x∈(-1,1), calculate the value of f(194). Express your answer as a single numerical value.

<reflection>
The given conditions are: f is defined on all real numbers; y = f(2x - 1) is odd; y = f(x + 1) is even; f(x) = e^x for x in (-1, 1). For an odd function g, the defining relation is g(-x) = -g(x).
If g(x) = f(2x - 1) is odd, then g(-x) = f(2(-x) - 1) = f(-2x - 1), so the correct relation is f(-2x - 1) = -f(2x - 1). The sign inside the argument is wrong.
Replace x by -x in g(x) = f(2x - 1) to obtain f(-2x - 1) = -f(2x - 1), then combine this with the even condition f(x + 1) = f(-x + 1) to derive a periodicity relation for f.
</reflection>
